raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On gfx1250, MLA prefill runs three small ops on different paths from gfx950: `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding` runs `forward_native` (about nine torch kernels), RMSNorm uses a gfx1250-only Triton branch, and the MLA KV rows go through `index_put`. aiter's cached-positions RoPE kernel and `rmsnorm2d_fwd` build and run on gfx1250 with the current gfx1250 aiter pin; the RMSNorm row-tail fix for N % 8 != 0 is ROCm/aiter#6348, which the pin includes. This PR extends the gfx950 paths for these three ops to gfx1250.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding`: on gfx1250 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, call `aiter.rope_cached_positions_2c_fwd_inplace` in place. The module stays sglang's because ROCm MLA decode paths read `cos_sin_cache`, which aiter's rope modules do not have. The kernel reads cos/sin without strides, so it gets contiguous query-dtype copies of the module's own `cos_sin_cache`, built on first use and rebuilt when the cache or the query dtype changes. `forward_native` is kept for calls with `offsets` and when `rl_on_policy_target` forces native rope. A key passed as its own query (the `IndexerKPool` K-only path) is rotated once, since the kernel loads both inputs before storing.
- RMSNorm: drop the gfx1250 Triton branch and use aiter `rmsnorm2d_fwd` / `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add`, as on other ROCm targets. This applies to every model on gfx1250 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, in prefill and decode.
- MLA KV rows: use `store_mla` / `read_mla` on gfx1250, as on gfx950.
- Update the rope factory and DeepSeek utils comments that said aiter rope does not build on gfx1250.
- Add a gfx1250-only test in `test/registered/rotary/test_rope_rocm.py` that compares the aiter RoPE path with `forward_native` (neox and GPT-J styles, strided q_pe/k_pe views shaped like the MLA callers, in-place output, cache growth, dtype change, a key passed as its own query, and the `forward_native` fallbacks).

gfx950 is unchanged. On gfx1250, RoPE now runs in place with query-dtype cos/sin, the same as the aiter rope module on gfx950. MLA decode RoPE on gfx1250 also moves to this kernel, except where #44459 fuses it into the decode kernel; the measurements below were taken with #44458 and #44459 applied, so this PR should land after #44459.

Validated on gfx1250 with Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4 at TP8.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 8-shot, 1319 questions, 3 runs:

| | Runs | Mean |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 0.944 / 0.939 / 0.938 | 0.940 |
| After | 0.945 / 0.935 / 0.939 | 0.940 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`bench_serving`, 8k input / 1k output, FP8 KV cache, aiter decode backend, page size 64.

| Concurrency | | Throughput per GPU (tok/s/GPU) | Interactivity (tok/s/user) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | Before | 442.3 | 104.7 | 262.3 | 9.55 |
| 4 | After | 443.2 | 104.7 | 238.8 | 9.55 |
| 4 | Change | +0.2% | 0.0% | -9.0% | 0.0% |
| 16 | Before | 1017.8 | 59.6 | 270.6 | 16.78 |
| 16 | After | 1038.1 | 60.7 | 248.0 | 16.49 |
| 16 | Change | +2.0% | +1.8% | -8.4% | -1.7% |
| 64 | Before | 1520.0 | 21.8 | 430.3 | 45.97 |
| 64 | After | 1568.2 | 22.4 | 411.0 | 44.59 |
| 64 | Change | +3.2% | +3.1% | -4.5% | -3.0% |

In the prefill profile (8192-token chunks, GPU kernel time excluding all-reduce, mean over 8 ranks), a chunk goes from 175.0 ms to 153.6 ms at concurrency 4. Elementwise kernels go from 25.2 to 10.0 ms and RMSNorm from 19.4 to 15.6 ms; the new RoPE kernel takes 1.0 ms. Decode kernel time is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing option changes.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

+        q_out, k_out = rope(positions, q_pe, k_pe)
+
+        self.assertEqual(q_out.data_ptr(), q_pe.data_ptr())
+        self.assertEqual(k_out.data_ptr(), k_pe.data_ptr())
+        # forward_native adds a leading dim on the neox path.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            q[..., 128:], q_ref.reshape(q_pe.shape), atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            kv[..., 512:], k_ref.reshape(k_pe.shape), atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2
+        )
+
+    def test_matches_native(self) -> None:
+        for is_neox in (False, True):
+            for num_tokens, num_heads in ((1, 16), (311, 8), (2048, 64)):
+                with self.subTest(is_neox=is_neox, num_tokens=num_tokens):
+                    self._run_case(is_neox, num_tokens, num_heads)
+
+    def test_rebuilds_after_cache_growth(self) -> None:
+        rope = self._small_rope()
+        q = torch.randn(4, 16, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        k = torch.randn(4, 1, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        rope(torch.arange(4, device="cuda"), q.clone(), k.clone())
+
+        old_cache = rope.cos_sin_cache
+        rope._ensure_cos_sin_cache_length(1024)
+        self.assertIsNot(rope.cos_sin_cache, old_cache)
+        positions = torch.tensor([0, 255, 600, 1000], device="cuda")
+        q_ref, k_ref = rope.forward_native(positions, q.clone(), k.clone())
+        q_out, k_out = rope(positions, q.clone(), k.clone())
+        self.assertIs(rope._aiter_cos_sin[0], rope.cos_sin_cache)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(q_out, q_ref, atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(k_out, k_ref, atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
+    def _small_rope(self) -> rope_variant.DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding:
+        return rope_variant.DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding(
+            64,
+            64,
+            256,
+            50000,
+            False,
+            1.0,
+            torch.bfloat16,
+            mscale=1.0,
+            mscale_all_dim=1.0,
+            device="cuda",
+        ).to("cuda")
+
+    def test_rebuilds_on_dtype_change(self) -> None:
+        rope = self._small_rope()
+        positions = torch.arange(4, device="cuda")
+        for dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            q = torch.randn(4, 16, 64, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+            k = torch.randn(4, 1, 64, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+            q_ref, k_ref = rope.forward_native(positions, q.clone(), k.clone())
+            q_out, k_out = rope(positions, q.clone(), k.clone())
+            self.assertEqual(rope._aiter_cos_sin[1].dtype, dtype)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(q_out, q_ref, atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(k_out, k_ref, atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
+    def test_offsets_use_native(self) -> None:
+        rope = self._small_rope()
+        positions = torch.arange(4, device="cuda")
+        q = torch.randn(4, 16, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        k = torch.randn(4, 1, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        offsets = torch.full((4,), 7, device="cuda")
+        q_ref, k_ref = rope.forward_native(positions, q.clone(), k.clone(), offsets)
+        q_out, k_out = rope(positions, q.clone(), k.clone(), offsets)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(q_out, q_ref, atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(k_out, k_ref, atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
+    def test_key_passed_as_its_own_query(self) -> None:
+        # IndexerKPool's K-only path passes the rope slice of the key twice.
+        rope = self._small_rope()
+        positions = torch.arange(4, device="cuda")
+        key = torch.randn(4, 1, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        k_rope = key[..., :64]
+        k_ref = rope.forward_native(positions, k_rope.clone(), k_rope.clone())[1]
+        rope(positions, k_rope, k_rope)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(key[..., :64], k_ref, atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
+    def test_force_native_keeps_native(self) -> None:
+        exec_ctx = SimpleNamespace(
+            deterministic=SimpleNamespace(rl_on_policy_target="fsdp")
+        )
+        with (
+            patch.object(rotary_base, "publish_role", return_value="rollout"),
+            patch.object(rotary_base, "get_exec", return_value=exec_ctx),
+        ):
+            rope = self._small_rope()
+        self.assertEqual(rope._forward_method, rope.forward_native)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
